author: fester
body: Type comparison answers THREE values, not two. A rechecker that cannot decide must say so: collapsing the undecided case into equal manufactures agreement it did not earn, and collapsing it into unequal manufactures a disagreement against a program that is fine. Both are worse than silence. docs/Designs/Active/Tools/IndependentRechecker.md section 6 is the rule.

author: fester
body: A definite difference in any component is a definite difference overall, so TyNeq outranks TyUnknown here: FunTy a r and FunTy b r differ whatever is unknown about r once a and b are known to differ.

author: fester
body: The atom `error` on the wire is not only ErrorTy: ir-emit-type has no arm for ProofTy, PropEqTy, TypeCon or TypeApply, and its `is otherwise` sends all four to the same spelling. Four distinct types and one failure type are indistinguishable here, so every one of them is undecided.

author: fester
body: A unit type is documented as transparent to its inner type at assignment boundaries, and the exact extent of that is not settled by the language docs. Answering Unknown rather than guessing is deliberate; do not "fix" it to Eq or Neq without a documented rule to cite. Resolving it by reading strip-unit-ty is the one move section 7 forbids.

author: fester
body: Equality is the wrong question in an argument position and using it there was this rechecker's first bug, caught by its own control: passing a value of `Integer between 0 and 20` to a plain `Integer` parameter is ordinary Codex, and equality called it a disagreement.

author: fester
body: A value flows from a narrower band into a wider one, never the reverse. The reverse direction is the one that matters and it stays a disagreement, which is what the compiler itself does -- an unproven range in a bounded slot is CDX2051, refused rather than guarded.

author: fester
body: Overflow mode is not a range, so a difference in mode is not a fit that can be decided by containment. Undecided rather than guessed.

author: fester
body: One type has two spellings on this wire and they meet each other. A sum or record type is emitted INLINE with its constructors where it stands on its own, but a RECURSIVE reference inside its own constructor field list is emitted as the truncated `(ctd "Expr" (args))`, deliberately: the emitter says re-emitting the fields caused exponential IR bloat on recursive types. So the constructor `Mul` carries a parameter typed as the inlined `(sum "Expr" ...)` while the same sum's own field list for `Mul` says `(ctd "Expr" (args))`. They denote one type and structural equality called them different, which reported four disagreements on `expr-calculator` and eleven on `final-batch-test` in the first full sweep, all of them this rechecker's own.

author: fester
body: Nominal identity is the right comparison for both spellings: same name and same type arguments is the same type. A different name still disagrees, so this widens nothing except across the spelling boundary.
